---
title: "Red flags"
date-modified: 2026-10-02
---

::: {.status}
**Version 0.1.** Failures reported by practitioners at ACLCA 2026. This list grows as members contribute cases; [send us yours](../get-involved.qmd).
:::

## Fabricated references and hyperlinks

**What happened:** citations that look plausible but do not exist. **Why it matters here:** the real literature on a new technology is thin, which makes invented citations more likely. **Do instead:** open every source before using it.

## Chemical equations that do not balance

**What happened:** AI-researched reaction equations were often not stoichiometrically balanced on the first pass. **Why it matters here:** every inventory value derived from them inherits the error. **Do instead:** balance and check equations yourself or with deterministic tools before they enter the model.

## Silent boundary mismatches

**What happened:** AI compared cradle-to-gate results against cradle-to-grave results, and studies with different allocation choices, without flagging the difference. **Do instead:** never accept an AI comparison of studies without confirming boundaries, functional units, and allocation match. Interpretation stays human-led.

## Confident mapping to the wrong dataset

**What happened:** suggested background datasets did not match the system modeled. **Why it matters here:** a novel material often has no correct match, and AI will pick something anyway. **Do instead:** choose proxies explicitly and document the rationale.

## Plausible explanations only expertise could catch

**What happened:** AI produced reasonable-sounding explanations for data discrepancies; only the practitioner's process knowledge kept a wrong one out of the report. **Do instead:** treat AI explanations as hypotheses to test. If nobody on the team can evaluate an explanation independently, it does not go in.

## Bench scale data scaled naively

**What happened:** models trained on lab data misled at plant scale, because heating, cooling, and catalyst dynamics do not scale linearly. **Do instead:** treat scale-up estimates as scenarios with ranges, grounded in engineering calculation or simulation.

## Inventory values generated from nothing

**What happened:** asked for a number it could not know, the AI produced one anyway. This was the most strongly condemned practice at the session. **Do instead:** collect the data, calculate it, use a disclosed proxy with uncertainty, or report the gap.
